scope: Read all 25 passages, overviews, periods, endings, overrides and identity notes. Independently checked selected claims in 9 of 20 sources. Bounded review, not full historical or border certification.

sourcesChecked.checked: Indexed original ORACC edition: exact opening, translation, Sennacherib sender, Sargon II reign and reported Urartian defeat. Public sample is correctly identified as Akkadian transliteration.
Direct excavation chronology: older circa 700 BCE attribution superseded by tree rings and five seed samples from separate pots supporting circa 800 BCE.
Direct object catalogue: circa 650 BCE, 4.3 centimetres, proposed sheath fitting and Cimmerian association; related possibly unfinished object supports only tentative local manufacture.
Direct original results: 15 of 16 individual calculus samples, sheep/goat/cattle identifications and qualified processing possibilities despite rare lactase-persistence variant.
Direct primary abstract: three children about six, two graves, circa 3300 to 3100 BCE, later covering mound and differences in pot/mat manufacture. Speculative disease causation omitted.
Direct primary conference paper pages 13 to 15: 43 well-described graves, separate wheels, chassis as bed or cover and Izobilnoe clay wheel copies.
Direct university research interview: absence of written source material is correctly scoped to Yamnaya communities; linguistic reconstruction is distinguished from attested text.
Indexed original primary review: skeletal indicators lack specificity, wagon transport offers alternatives, and comparative evidence is needed. Direct PMC request returned a browser challenge.
Indexed original PubMed abstract: Anthony, Trautmann and Heyd, May 2026, argument for earlier Yamnaya riding based on multiple evidence types. Card presents a disputed research position.

limits: Eleven other sources not independently reopened; author evidence and access notes retained.
Imported Cimmerian dates are not treated as attested lifetime; archaeological ethnic attributions remain qualified.
Yamnaya is identified as an archaeological tradition with regional differences, not a kingdom.
